static_traits.name: Zhang Jie
static_traits.family_status: Both parents active in the church choir
static_traits.social_status: Has friends to confide in, but they do not quite understand the depth of his guilt about missing church; Interpersonal relationships not yet affected
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not received counseling or treatment in the past; no similar church-attendance-related problems before
static_traits.language_features: Expressing clearly, with a positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Because I have not been to church for a while, I keep feeling I am a terrible child, and this thought causes me pain and guilt.
basic_info.core_demands: I sought counseling because guilt and negative self-perceptions have affected my mental health and caused inner pain.
growth_experiences: Religious atmosphere of the family of origin: the parents have long been active in a church choir; the family values participation in church and community activities; this value orientation influenced their understanding of the 'good child' standard (seeing attendance at worship as an important responsibility).

special_situations.event: Thinking on Sundays that church service is underway while I have not attended
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not attend important family and community activities, it means I am an irresponsible, terrible child
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to rationalize absence with 'work is busy' to reduce guilt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a bad kid; I have disappointed my parents and the church

special_situations.event: Recalls that her parents have long been active in the church choir and expect family members to participate
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot meet parents' religious and group-participation standards, it proves I am not good enough and unworthy of recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids talking with parents about absence, keeps distance to avoid disappointing them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have disappointed my parents' expectations

special_situations.event: Talking with friends about not going to church; friends think he is 'overreacting/just too busy'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others think my worries are not serious, it means my feelings are not understood, and I really did wrong
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further self-reproach, focusing on others' uncomprehending feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not understand my guilt; I may really be terrible

special_situations.event: Recalling having missed church services several times in a row
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once I cannot keep attending services, it equals complete failure, becoming a bad person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Judging oneself by all-or-nothing standards, using self-blame to push oneself to church
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed; I am a bad person

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by parents and the group as a 'good child' and to maintain moral consistency
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing parents, being judged as a 'bad person', thus losing recognition and acceptance
defense_goal: Maintaining a moral self-image through rationalizing absence and self-reproach
Avoids direct communication with parents to avoid facing disappointment and judgment

object_relations.object_representation: Judges with high expectations who may be disappointed (parents/church community)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the reasons for absence from church or advised to communicate with parents
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes honest communication will immediately bring the parents' disappointment and judgment
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Calm tone, emphasizes being busy with work and responsibility pressure, downplays emotional content, avoiding deeper discussion of the feasibility of communicating with her parents.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: On Sundays, when thinking about the ongoing service
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating missing worship with 'I am a bad person' (self-labeling)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Briefly acknowledging guilt, but quickly displacing to work tasks and fact lists, reducing emotional expression.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Facing others' incomprehension of his guilt (e.g., friends thinking he overreacts)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Taking others' incomprehension as negation of self-worth, reinforcing self-blame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming language toward one's own flaws, avoiding expressing disappointment or anger at others' feedback.

manifestations: Experiences strong guilt when weighing choices between work and religious obligations
Viewing missing worship as violating internalized moral standards
Binds the meaning of being a 'good child' solely to fixed religious behaviors (attending worship)
Overlooking one's other contributions to the community and family
outcomes: Negating the value of positive behaviors

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently judges oneself with 'a good child should attend worship'
Directly labeling oneself 'a bad person/a terrible child' for not attending worship

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Worrying about disappointing parents and not communicating with them, instead intensifying self-blame
Not seeking external clarification when guilt rises, choosing to endure

exception_events.target_problem: When thinking on Sundays about not going to church, the client usually develops strong guilt and self-labels with 'I am a terrible child', leading to low mood.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At the time when he previously donated instruments to the local school and organized in-store community events, his parents felt proud of his actions; he saw his positive impact on community and family, different from his previous practice of binding self-worth entirely to church attendance.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different approach — actively participating in community support and charity; different support — parents explicitly expressing recognition and pride; different understanding — expanding the 'good child' standard to include various forms of contribution.

positive_force: Has a stable professional role and community contributions (organizes activities, donates instruments to local schools)
Able to reflect rationally and willing to seek professional help (reality testing, strong counseling motivation)
Has a friends support network (not fully understanding, but confidable)
The family recognizes their positive behavior on the value dimension (parents are proud of their public-welfare behavior)
negative_force: Internalizing religious participation into a rigid 'should' standard
Tends toward personalization and mental filtering, ignoring own positive evidence
Excessive self-blame and self-labeling lower self-worth
Avoids communicating with parents, maintaining imagined judgment and disappointment
All-or-nothing self-evaluation, prone to seeing one absence as total failure

target_behavior.behavior: Self-blame and guilt (self-labels with 'I am a bad child')
antecedent: Thinking on Sundays about not yet attending church service
Seeing reminders of parents or church-related activities
Talking with friends about missing church
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing family religious norms as absolute self-evaluation standards, and assessing self-worth in all-or-nothing terms
target_behavior.function: Maintaining moral consistency through self-blame, temporarily avoiding the Anxiety of communicating with parents
target_behavior.consequence: Daily low mood and Anxiety, decreased sense of self-worth, but Work performance not yet affected

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids communicating with parents about the fact and feelings of missing church
antecedent: Anticipating that parents may be disappointed or judgmental
When advised to communicate with parents
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being negated and losing recognition, tending to personalize absence as hurting parents
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential embarrassment and conflict, reducing Anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Guilt persists, lacking realistic feedback and support, maintaining the problem cycle
